source_snapshot.procedure: Attempt power-on with one cabled PSU, add PSUs one by one and check power-on; boot the full population to OS; remove the first slot's cable and module and observe normal versus shutdown; restore module/cable, check PSU LED, and repeat for every remaining PSU.
source_snapshot.criteria: System should be unable to power on with 2 PSU; system should not shut down when one PSU is hot-removed.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO correctly makes physical PSU/cable work manual, but assumes reduced-population boot success and hot-remove continuity despite the opposite two-PSU criterion.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly identifies the minimum-population contradiction and requires redundancy/load/service authority before any power action.

old_problem: The Procedure seeks the minimum working PSU population beginning at one and later expects one-module hot-remove continuity, while Criterion 1 says the system must be unable to power on with two PSUs. It also fails to distinguish power-off population changes from live insertion, and gives no fitted topology, feed-group budget, service sequence, LED/event oracle or recovery.
disposition_reason: Research can define evidence and safety but cannot make the core acceptance choice. Standard redundancy states distinguish fully redundant, degraded/lost, and non-redundant sufficient or insufficient resources; they do not make one PSU bootable while two PSUs are unbootable for this unspecified platform. A complete parameterized draft separates zero/one/two/full cold-start trials from full-population per-slot live service, yet it remains BLOCKED until the Project owner corrects the contradictory expected-result matrix and says whether `add one by one` occurs only with power removed or is an approved live insertion. Physical cable/module actions, per-feed capacity and recovery are also mandatory.
decision_basis: XLSX row 807, physical adjacent row 808, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. No duplicate Wistron-BMC-00097-V004 exists.

The formal queue's sequences 22-56 already belong to the integrity-validated adopted set, so after this case the next missing identity is sequence 57: Functionality row 1015 / Wistron-BMC-00305-V002 / variant 5653b172749853db.

IPMI generic redundancy state 0Bh distinguishes Fully Redundant, Redundancy Lost/Degraded, Non-redundant Sufficient Resources and Non-redundant Insufficient Resources. Those states support an evidence matrix but do not define a platform's minimum cold-start population or rated load.

A system may have adequate aggregate nameplate wattage yet lack an allowed feed, phase, PSU firmware, population symmetry or current headroom. Conversely, `unable with 2 PSU` could reflect an unstated Project topology. Neither outcome may be guessed or silently corrected to `able`.

Cold-start population tests require power-off reconfiguration and a separate complete boot attempt for each authorized population. Live cable/module removal tests failover under load. One cannot substitute for the other, and a powered-down replacement cannot PASS hot-remove coverage.

Disconnecting an AC feed and physically extracting a module can produce different BMC events and load-transfer timing. The exact vendor cable/latch ordering, hot-plug support, remaining feed-group capacity and same-serial restoration are safety-critical.

ED-02 preserves identity; ED-03/ED-13 prohibit guessed BMC semantics; ED-06 separates power mechanisms; ED-15 requires SPEC proof for N/A; ED-17/ED-25 keep physical actions manual; ED-18/ED-30 prohibit invented power limits; ED-19 protects logs; ED-22 preserves real hardware state; ED-29 requires complete state/OS Ready; ED-33 through ED-38 require source correction and owner verdict before execution.

test_case.test_name: PSU minimum-population cold start and per-slot live redundancy — BLOCKED DRAFT
test_case.purpose: After the Project resolves the population contradiction, independently verify every authorized zero/one/two/full cold-start state and every fitted PSU's approved cable/module live-service path, including load transfer, host continuity, physical LED/BMC/SEL behavior and complete same-module/feed redundancy restoration.
required_package: Signed zero/one/two/.../full PSU population matrix for the exact chassis/backplane/PSU firmware and configured hardware load, stating supported versus intentionally rejected cold power-on, POST/boot/OS Ready outcome, timeout and expected evidence for each state

Explicit interpretation of `add PSU one by one`: power-off reconfiguration followed by independent cold starts, vendor-supported live insertion, or both as separately passing checkpoints; no transition is inferred

Fitted PSU topology: logical/physical slot, module model/serial/firmware/rating/derating, FRU/PMBus/BMC sensor, AC cable/PDU outlet/feed/phase/group, physical LED meanings and raw SEL/redundancy event map

Project redundancy/power budget for every tested population and each single-slot removal: measured demand, maximum approved workload, survivor/group capacity, sharing/imbalance and rail tolerances, failover timing and host `normal` definition

Vendor-approved power-off population-change and live-service SOPs with cable/module/latch ordering, hot-plug support, connector/ESD inspection, one-module limit, same-serial/feed restoration, operator, aborts and OOB recovery
Read-only PDU/PMBus/rail/BMC/SEL/host/fan/thermal monitoring, visual LED evidence, full evidence export/hash and per-action approval
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED — DO NOT EXECUTE. Once a signed population matrix resolves one-versus-two PSU acceptance, preserve/hash logs and inventory every slot/serial/feed. Cold-start lane: with power safely removed, a qualified operator configures each approved population, records physical identities, then performs one bounded cold power-on and verifies the exact expected reject or complete OFF-to-ON-to-OS-Ready result; power down by the approved method before changing population. Restore the full fitted configuration and prove full redundancy. Live-service lane: under the approved load, calculate the affected feed group's survivor capacity, display the exact cable/module order, expected redundancy/LED/events, aborts and recovery, and obtain immediate confirmation. The operator services one mapped PSU only; automation records PDU/PMBus/rails/share/redundancy/SEL/host continuity. Reinsert the same serial/feed, secure it and restore full sharing/redundancy before another slot. Never infer Criterion 1 is a typo, hot-add where unsupported, remove multiple PSUs, use aggregate capacity only, clear logs, auto-retry power-on/removal or issue a DUT verdict.
test_case.expected_result: Cannot be authoritative until the signed matrix states which zero/one/two/full populations must reject power-on or reach OS Ready and whether add-one-by-one is cold or live. Thereafter every cold-start result must match its exact population oracle, and every approved live removal must create the mapped absence/input/redundancy event while remaining feed groups stay within limits and host/BMC remain in the specified state. Physical LED/status/SEL and same-serial reinsertion must match Project policy, followed by full feed, share, redundancy, thermal and OS/BMC recovery.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS while the one-versus-two population contradiction or add-one-by-one state remains unresolved. After correction, PASS requires every matrix population attempted once in the approved power state, exact expected power/POST/OS Ready outcome, full baseline restoration, then every fitted supported slot serviced one at a time with measured group headroom, mapped physical LED/BMC/SEL/redundancy state, stable rails and host continuity, same-serial/feed restoration and full redundancy before advancing. Assuming `able`, skipping unsupported populations without SPEC, powered replacement claimed as live failover, aggregate-only capacity, wrong feed/event, unexpected shutdown, connector/thermal/rail anomaly, missing visual evidence, retry or incomplete recovery cannot pass.
safety_gate: Current gate is CLOSED. Do not connect/disconnect a PSU cable, extract/insert a module, issue power control or clear logs until the Project signs the population and service-state matrix.

A qualified operator performs all cabling/module/latch actions and physical LED checks. Verify exact serial/slot/feed, de-energization where required, hot-service support, connector condition and ESD controls.
Cold-start population reconfiguration and live service are different phases. Power must be in the exact vendor state before each; never transition implicitly between them.

Before live removal, use measured current demand and Project derating for the specific remaining feed group. One module maximum absent; abort on overload/imbalance, rail instability, arcing/heat, wrong event, unplanned power loss, fan/thermal anomaly or OOB/host loss.
Preserve first-failure SEL/BMC/PDU/host evidence. Do not automatically retry a failed boot/removal, change another slot or power-cycle after ambiguity.
Restore and secure the same module and feed, verify FRU/PMBus/LED/rails/share/redundancy/thermal/host health and obtain owner release before any next action.
expected_evidence: Dated signed minimum-population and add-one-by-one decision, exact Source Key/variant and chassis/backplane/PSU/firmware/tool identities
Zero/one/two/full fitted-population, slot/serial/feed/group/PDU/PMBus/LED/SDR/SEL topology and rated/derated power budget
Per-population power-off configuration photos/operator records plus OFF-to-power/POST/OS Ready or expected-rejection timeline and logs
Full-population baseline and per-slot live action approval, measured survivor capacity, PDU/PMBus/rail/share/redundancy/fan/thermal/host traces
Genuine physical LED/connector evidence and raw BMC/SEL assertion/deassertion mapped to each cable/module action
Same-serial/feed restoration, full redundancy/share and OS/BMC health, unexpected events and engineer-owned per-population/per-slot/overall verdicts
test_case.recovery: Present recovery cannot authorize action before the population matrix is corrected. The approved plan must stop immediately on an unexpected power state, overload, rail/thermal/connector anomaly or lost management; preserve the first evidence; remove further stimulus; and let the power owner choose safe isolation. Restore the exact module/cable/feed only through the vendor procedure, or use the pre-approved controlled shutdown when live restoration is unsafe. Do not retry or touch another slot. Verify physical connectors, FRU/PMBus, rails, sharing, full redundancy, temperatures, BMC and complete OS Ready before closure.

source_conflict.reason: A one-PSU power-on exploration and blanket `unable with 2 PSU` criterion cannot both define PASS without an unstated topology rule. Cold add versus live add is also unspecified; no standard or approved ED selects the intended matrix.

blocked.reason: The contradiction controls both verdict and whether the remaining power path is safe. Physical execution before source correction could overload a feed or power off the DUT while still producing no authoritative result.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Defines generic redundancy states and power-supply/power-unit sensor/SEL structure used for evidence; it does not prescribe the DUT's minimum population, load capacity or hot-service support.

external_authorities.title: Intel Server Board S1200V3RP Technical Product Specification
external_authorities.application: Illustrates platform-specific differentiation of Fully Redundant, Redundancy Lost/Degraded, Non-redundant Sufficient and Insufficient Resources. It is evidence that exact platform TPS is required, not an oracle for this unidentified DUT.

project_authority: Only the exact chassis/backplane/PSU and Project power owners may resolve minimum population, permitted transitions and safe capacity. Their signed decision cannot silently rewrite Master history, claim powered-down replacement as hot failover, waive a source population without SPEC, substitute aggregate wattage for feed analysis or confer PASS without all required physical and telemetry evidence.
